new_statements.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress is predictable.
new_statements.citation: Aeschliman, Ulys. 1992 (Dec.). Nobnob Organised Phonology Data [Nobonob (Garuh) Language [GAW], Madang Province]. Ukarumpa: SIL PNG. 4 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 42396 (draft, posted as is; PDF printed 1 Sept 2004).
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only statement is that stress is predictable (i.e. non-contrastive); the source does not say on which syllable it falls, and none of the ~150 example words or the transcribed text passage is marked for stress. Tone and length are listed in the section heading but nothing is said about tone; long vowels and long consonants are written orthographically (aa, ee, ii, oo, uu; underlined p t k).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (the OPD is a citation-form phonology data sheet); no phrase-level remarks. The document is a 4-page SIL PNG 'Organised Phonology Data' summary, not a full phonology.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD is headed 'Nobonob (Garuh) Language [GAW], Madang - Madang Province; Mabuso Stock; Hanseman Family; villages Nagada, Betip, Amron, Haven, Balepa, Belan, Butelkud' = nobo1238 exactly. It notes that one consonant 'is pronounced as a voiceless dental lenis aspirated plosive in some dialects' but names no dialect. Z'graggen's Garuh (language no. 7 / C28) and Dempwolff's Nupanob/Bawaipa/Misdao are the same language under older names.
